title: Count only independent agreement
statement: Treat a finding as settled only when independent methods or sources reach it.
example: One faulty item was caught both by a blind solve that guessed it 4 times out of 4 and by a separate reading of its options' length and phrasing.
detail: A review of 269 teaching-video transcripts, split into 9 batches, treated findings that recurred across independent batches as high-confidence and a technique seen once as a candidate, not a rule (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/g3-reading-red-team/references/IES-CORPUS-REVIEW-2026-08-05.md`, lines 13-18). In one build, two agents grepped a file holding a NUL byte without the flag that reads such files, both got nothing, and both reported that no filter existed: true, as it turned out, but reached by an invalid method twice (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g3-reading/iteration-3/BUILD-RULES.md`, lines 1104-1117). A red-team addendum calls two independent instruments landing on one item the strongest signal in the document, and the argument for running both. A finding seen once, carried from another project, or reached twice by the same source, model or method is a single candidate.
against: It rests on one case. a decision matrix keeps duplicate rulings instead of merging them, treating repetition across sources as evidence of consensus across authorities (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0242-decision-matrix-judgment-corpus.qmd`).
